_about: SYNTHETIC test crag. Every name, person, route and coordinate is invented; the coordinates sit in the open South Atlantic, far from any land. Sun windows and sunrise/sunset are hand-set so the shade arithmetic can be checked by hand.

crag.subtitle: A fictional crag used to test this skill
approach_tips: Most approaches are steep: use the dry streambed rather than scrambling straight up.
Park only in the marked lay-by; the verge is soft after rain.

contents_title: The four sectors at a glance

cover.blurb: A synthetic guide used to test the crag-guidebook skill: 4 sectors, 12 invented routes, calculated June shade, and field notes from an invented visit. Nothing here is real.

front_pages.title: Important before you go
front_pages.html:
Read this first
  1. Shade times are calculated and approximate. They come from each wall's aspect and the sun's position; a first-hand observation overrides them where marked.
  2. Wear a helmet. Loose blocks at the top of several routes (A. Visitor).
  3. Anchors. Most anchors are two bolts with plain rings.
  4. Approaches. Use the dry streambed.

front_pages.title: Sources and method
front_pages.html:
Why this guide exists

It exists to test the skill. The spine source is the invented Example Database; the invented Example Printed Guide supplies local names and one topo.

What this guide is not

A survey. Nothing here has been checked on the ground except the marked field notes.

front_pages.title: Grades, stars, names and shade
front_pages.html:
Stars and the top pick

Stars 0–3 from the spine. ♪ is the visitor's personal top pick.

Local names

Names marked † are reconstructed from the Latin name and may differ from the rock.

Shade — when you can climb

Shade is the complement of the calculated sun window within daylight (07:00–19:00 on 15 June).

front_pages.title: Hollowmere Gorge
front_pages.html:
A short invented gorge with four sectors on alternating banks of a north–south stream.

Bolt condition

One of four sectors flagged, one caution, two unknown. Unknown is not a clean bill of health.

sectors.name: Lichen Slab
sectors.intro: A friendly slab on the west bank, first on the left as you enter.
sectors.gear: 8 quickdraws; a 60 m rope is enough.
sectors.approach: From the lay-by, follow the streambed for 2 minutes.

sectors.name: Owl Buttress
sectors.intro: A steep buttress on the east bank with the best rock in the gorge.
sectors.approach: Cross the stream at the stepping stones.
field_notes: Flat, shaded base; good for a group.

sectors.intro: A deep, south-facing corner that never sees the sun in June.
sectors.approach: Continue up the streambed past Owl Buttress.

sectors.name: Heron Wall

shade_override.headline: Shade (observed 2026-06-01): until about 10:00 · afternoon not observed
shade_override.sentence: By calculation the wall faces W and would stay in shade until about 13:00. That is not what happens. On 2026-06-01 the sun was on the wall by about 10:00; the afternoon was not observed (A. Visitor). Treat the calculated aspect as unreliable.

sectors.intro: The tallest wall, high on the east bank.
sectors.warn: Wader needs rebolting: two spinning bolts reported.
sectors.approach: Steep scramble from the end of the streambed.
